about: What the workbench bar does, once for both viewers: Storybook's Playwright suite (packages/components/test/visual/workbench-scenarios.spec.mjs) and Widgetbook's widget tests (packages/solar_flutter/widgetbook/test/workbench_scenarios_test.dart) run every scenario here against their own bar, each through a small driver over a fake of the HTTP contract (docs/engineering/architecture.md, The workbench). A step or an expectation a driver lacks fails that driver. Words may differ between the bars; the facts shown may not.

A value { "$fixture": "<name>", ... } is a copy of fixtures.<name> with the object's other keys put over it, resolved in turn. The string "$platform" is the bar's own platform (web in Storybook, flutter in Widgetbook) and "$other" the other one, as a value or as an object's key. packages/codegen/test/workbench-scenarios.test.mjs checks every scenario against the vocabulary below.

Every control offered must be one of vocabulary.actions or vocabulary.named (or, on one platform alone, vocabulary.platformActions: controls the scenarios never name): at the last expectation, and at any naming enabled, disabled or absent, the actions offered are exactly enabled and disabled together. The controls counted are the dialog's while the Inspect dialog is open (the bar hidden behind it counts no more, and nor does the component drawn in its preview), else the bar's. A scenario that presses, chooses, confirms or cancels names the calls it expects last, even none.

outlined and point need a component whose layers both viewers can locate in the preview (dialog.layer): the web finds every layer by its selector, Flutter only a component SolarLayers draws (keyed <prefix>.<layer>), so those scenarios use Option Card, and the rest use Button. Where a viewer cannot locate a component's layers (Flutter's Material-based widgets, Button among them), its dialog shows the selected layer's name beside the preview instead of an outline, and takes no pointing: that is a platform test's, never a shared scenario's.

fake.health: false: nothing answers on the port (GET /health fails). Default true.
fake.startingTimes: how many times GET /status answers 503 (still starting) before it answers. Default 0.
fake.component: the component whose Playground the bar is drawn in (its name as the Status and the Inspection give it). Default Button.
fake.status: the Status GET /status answers, until an answer or a setStatus step changes it.
fake.inspection: the Inspection GET /component answers (the HTTP contract: axes, variants with their parts, each layer with its parent, each layer with its selector, each cell with its value, origin, reason and total, each scope with its plain label, count, wins, winsLabel and current), its variant set to the one asked. Its layer and class names are the real component's, since each viewer draws the preview from its own oracle.
fake.inspectionFor: { <variant index>: keys put over inspection where GET /component asks for that variant } (a variant that draws other layers). Default {}.
fake.controls: the Playground's values the bar is given, by control (what Report sends as controls). Default {}.
fake.answers: by route (status, component, set, keep, undo, approve, unapprove/preview, unapprove, report, send): { answer, status, events, hold } or { refuse: { status, error }, events, hold }. The route's events are delivered first; where hold is true, the answer then waits for a release step; then status (where given) becomes what GET /status answers, and the answer is sent: answer, the body (omitted, the Status now), or the refusal. A GET route takes refuse alone. A POST route not listed fails the scenario; a key not named here fails it too.

steps.press: presses the button of this name, which must be enabled: in the dialog where it is open, else in the bar. A Layer is the tree item, a Cell the property row.
steps.choose: { select, option }: opens the Select labelled select (an Axis: the axis's Select) and chooses the one option whose words contain option, or of several, the one whose words are option.
steps.confirm: true: confirms the Confirmation Dialog open.
steps.cancel: true: cancels the Confirmation Dialog open.
steps.type: { field, text }: replaces a field's text: "reason", the pending edit's reason; "note", Report's note; "agentNote", the note Send to agent carries with the failing checks; or "filter", the editor's Filter tokens.
steps.escape: a field (as type names them): presses Escape in it, which in a filter holding text clears it and leaves the dialog open.
steps.point: a layer: clicks (taps) the preview at a point of that layer's box that none of the layers inside it (by parent) covers, found as dialog.layer says.
steps.event: { type, message? }: the service sends this event (busy, changed or failed); the step ends once the bar has asked for the events after it.
steps.setStatus: a Status: what GET /status answers from now on.
steps.release: a route: the answer held there (hold) is sent.

expect.calls: the POSTs sent so far, in order, exactly: [route, body].
expect.reads: the reads sent so far other than GET /events, in order, exactly: ["health"], ["status"], ["component", { name, variant }].
expect.absent: actions not offered (redundant: an expectation naming enabled, disabled or absent, and every scenario's last, also checks that the actions offered are exactly enabled and disabled together).
expect.options: { <Select or Axis>: { enabled, disabled, chosen } }: the options that control offers are exactly enabled and disabled together, each entry naming one option by a fact its words contain (or a list of facts they all contain; of several options, the one whose words are the fact); chosen, a fact the chosen option's words contain.
expect.filter: the text the editor's Filter tokens holds, exactly.
expect.editorUnder: a cell: the editor (dialog.Editor) sits in the Properties table right under that cell's row, above the next row.
expect.outlined: a layer: the preview's outline (dialog."Selected layer outline") sits on that layer's box, to a pixel.
expect.shows: facts shown, in the bar or the dialog open: each a short phrase, not a sentence.
expect.oneError: exactly one error is shown (in the dialog where it is open, else in the bar), and it contains this fact.
expect.noError: true: no error is shown (in the dialog where it is open, else in the bar).

named.about: Actions named by a word and a name the inspection gives: "Axis state", "Layer label", "Cell radius". Each is one control.
named.Axis: the Select choosing the value of this variant axis (inspection.axes), in the dialog's header; its options the axis's values.
named.Layer: the Layers tree's item for this layer.
named.Cell: the Properties table's row for this cell of the selected layer; pressing it opens the cell's editor right under it (Apply to, Filter tokens, Change to).

dialog.about: Inspect opens a dialog over the page. The drivers find its parts by these names alone, never by looks: on the web by role and accessible name (or the attribute named), in Flutter by the widget named, or by a Semantics widget with exactly this label. Tasks building a dialog must give it these. Escape in an open Select closes that Select alone (the web driver reads a Select's options by opening it).
dialog.Inspect <component>: the dialog: web, role="dialog" with aria-modal and the accessible name "Inspect <component>" ("Inspect Button"); Flutter, a Semantics(label: "Inspect <component>") around the whole layer. Every part below is inside it.
dialog.Close: web, a button named "Close"; Flutter, a SolarIconButton whose semanticLabel is "Close" (or a SolarButton reading Close).
dialog.Axis <name>: a Select on both: web, a combobox whose name starts with the axis's name; Flutter, a SolarSelect labelled exactly the axis's name. Each option is labelled by the value; a value no drawn variant pairs with the other choices is a disabled option (web, aria-disabled; Flutter, a SolarSelectOption with enabled false).
dialog.Layers: the tree: web, role="tree" named "Layers", each layer a treeitem whose accessible name is the layer's name, alone or followed by a space and its marks ("hidden here"); Flutter, a Semantics(label: "Layers") around one SolarTreeItem per layer, labelled likewise, onSelect null where disabled.
dialog.Properties: the table under the heading "<layer>: properties": web, role="table" named "Properties", each row holding one button whose accessible name is the cell's name followed by a space and the rest of the row; Flutter, a Semantics(label: "Properties") around one Semantics(button: true, label: the same words) per row, enabled false where disabled. The editor sits inside it, right under the chosen row.
dialog.Editor: the chosen cell's editor, titled "<layer> · <cell>": web, role="group" with that accessible name; Flutter, a Semantics(label: "<layer> · <cell>"). Top to bottom: Apply to, Filter tokens, Change to, and the why line.
dialog.Apply to: the editor's Select of the scopes: web, a combobox whose name starts "Apply to"; Flutter, a SolarSelect labelled "Apply to", an option's words its label and helper. Each option reads "<label>: changes <count> of <total> variants", the one marked current followed by " (set here now)"; a scope with wins is disabled and also says "a narrower rule (<winsLabel>) decides this variant". The narrowest enabled scope is chosen.
dialog.Filter tokens: a SOLAR SearchField between Apply to and Change to: web, named "Filter tokens" (aria-label); Flutter, a SolarSearchField whose semanticLabel is "Filter tokens". It matches a token whose name or value contains its text, ignoring case; keywords and none are always listed. It starts at the current token's family (its name less the last segment: color.action.primary.bg) where that family matches at least one of the cell's choices, and empty otherwise (and for none, a keyword or a raw value); it starts so again on another cell, layer or variant and after a set. Escape in it, holding text, clears it and does not close the dialog.
dialog.Change to: the editor's Select: web, a combobox whose name starts "Change to"; Flutter, a SolarSelect labelled "Change to", an option's words its label and helper. Its options: the tokens the filter matches, at most 8, each with its value, the current entry's marked "current"; where more match, then a disabled option "…and <N> more: filter to narrow"; then the keywords and none. Its helper says "<tokens matched> of <all tokens>"; where no token matches it is disabled and says "No token matches".
dialog.why: the editor's last line: "Figma draws <entry>", "a rule at <the current scope's label> sets <entry>: <reason>", or "the shared defaults set <entry>: <reason>".
dialog.Preview: the component drawn: web, the element with aria-label="Preview", whose first element child is the component's root; Flutter, a Semantics(label: "Preview") around it. Controls inside it are the component's: never the dialog's, never counted.
dialog.Selected layer outline: the outline over the selected layer: web, the element with aria-label="Selected layer outline", its border box the layer's box; Flutter, a Semantics(label: "Selected layer outline") whose rect is the layer's.
dialog.Pending edit: the strip along the foot while this component's edit is pending: web, role="region" named "Pending edit"; Flutter, a Semantics(label: "Pending edit"). Keep, Undo, Reason, Agent note and Send to agent are inside it. It reads "<layer> · <cell>, for <scope label> (<count> variants): <was> → <new>", the scope the inspection's with the pending key.
dialog.read-only: while an edit is pending, the dialog says "One edit at a time: Keep or Undo the pending edit below first." (this component's) or "One edit at a time: Keep or Undo the pending edit in <component>'s Playground first." (another's); while an action runs the preview says "Regenerating…".
dialog.stale layer: where the variant chosen does not draw the layer in view, the dialog selects root; Change to and Report then name root.
dialog.error: an error while the dialog is open is shown in it: web, role="alert"; Flutter, a Text keyed WorkbenchBar.errorKey.
dialog.layer: a layer of the component drawn in the preview, for point and outlined: web, the element a case marks data-layer="<layer>", else the one the layer's selector (inspection) finds under the component's root, the Preview's first element child (& the root itself); Flutter, the widget whose key is <prefix>.<layer> (solar_layers.dart), found by its ending ".<layer>".
dialog.plural: Each "variants" above is "variant" after the number 1.

serial.about: The routes the service runs one at a time (session.mjs's serial). Unless the scenario gives the route's events itself, the fake sends busy (message "working: <route>", which GET /status answers as busy until the route has answered) when the request arrives, then, once the answer is decided, failed (with the refusal's error) where it refuses, and changed, before it answers.
